ristretto.description: A short cut of espresso. Syrupy, sweet, finished before it thins.
method: Warm a small cup, 45–60 ml.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 18–22 ml. Stop while the stream is still syrupy.
Serve at once.
ristretto.proTip: Ristretto is a shorter espresso, not a small normale.
ristretto.serve: 45–60 ml cup. Within seconds of the pour.

doppio-ristretto.description: Two ristrettos in one cup. Dense body, layered crema, concentrated sweetness.
method: Warm a 60–75 ml cup.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 36–44 ml. Stop before the flow turns thin.
Serve while the crema still sits.
doppio-ristretto.proTip: If one side runs faster, fix the puck before you touch the grinder.
doppio-ristretto.serve: 60–75 ml cup. Not a large demitasse.

espresso.description: The house shot. About 30–35 ml — crema, aroma, a short finish.
method: Warm a 50–70 ml cup.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Serve at once.
espresso.proTip: Taste the shot before you chase the clock.

double-espresso.description: Two shots in one cup. More body, a longer finish.
method: Warm a 70–90 ml cup.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 60–70 ml.
Serve at once.
double-espresso.proTip: A doppio that tastes flat in milk was flat on its own.

triple-espresso.description: Three shots, one cup. Strong, aromatic, drunk fast.
method: Warm a 130–150 ml cup.
Each puck even: distribute, level, tamp straight.
Pull three shots, 90–105 ml in total.
Serve while the aroma is still up.
triple-espresso.proTip: The third pull should not run faster than the first.

quad-espresso.description: Four shots. Maximum espresso in a short cup.
method: Warm a 160–180 ml cup.
Each puck even: distribute, level, tamp straight.
Pull four shots, 120–140 ml in total.
Serve. Do not let it wait.
quad-espresso.proTip: Volume waits worse than a single. Watch the flow, then the pass.

espresso-lungo.description: The same puck, pulled longer from the machine. More open, drier — not water in the cup.
method: Warm a 70–90 ml cup.
Grind on demand. Even puck.
Extract 50–65 ml from the machine. No water after.
Serve. It should taste more open than espresso.
espresso-lungo.proTip: Espresso lungo is a longer pull, not an espresso topped up.

short-black.description: A straight espresso, black, in a small warm cup. The Australian name for the same shot.
method: Warm a 50–70 ml cup.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Serve black. Do not lengthen it.
short-black.proTip: Cup heat and a fresh shot. Not more volume.

americano.description: Espresso lengthened with hot water. The aroma opens; the cup stays bright.
method: Put 120–150 ml hot water in a warm 180–220 ml cup.
Pull 30–35 ml espresso.
Pour the shot into the water. Stir once if you need to.
Serve hot.
americano.proTip: Water you would drink. For more body, a double into the cup while the shot is still running — not a finished shot topped up.

long-black.description: Water first, espresso last. Similar volume to americano, more crema on top.
method: Hot water in a warm 160–200 ml cup first.
Pull 30–35 ml espresso over the water.
Leave the crema. Do not stir unless you must.
Serve hot.
long-black.proTip: The drink is the order: water first, espresso last.

red-eye.description: Filter coffee with one espresso in it. More body, still a brewed cup.
method: Pour 160–190 ml fresh brew into a warm 200–240 ml cup.
Pull 30–35 ml espresso.
Add the shot to the brew. Stir once if you need to.
Serve hot.
red-eye.proTip: The brew is the drink. Hot water instead of coffee makes an americano.

black-eye.description: Filter coffee with two espressos. Heavier than a Red Eye — still brewed, not a large americano.
method: Pour 150–180 ml fresh brew into a warm 220–260 ml cup.
Pull two shots, about 30–35 ml each.
Add both to the brew. Stir once if you need to.
Serve hot. Do not stretch it into a bigger cup.
black-eye.proTip: Brewed coffee with espresso force — not a long black with extra shots.

lungo.description: A longer extraction, coarser than espresso. Softer body, a drier edge. Not espresso plus water.
method: Warm a 180–220 ml cup.
Grind a step coarser than espresso. Slightly lighter dose if the basket allows.
Extract 130–180 ml from the machine.
Serve. Softer than espresso, a little more bitter.
lungo.proTip: Change the extraction. Do not dilute a finished espresso.

caffe-crema.description: Swiss long pull. Golden crema, 90–120 ml from the machine, softer than espresso.
method: Warm a 120–150 ml cup.
Grind coarser than espresso so it can run longer without harshness.
Extract 90–120 ml into the cup. No water after.
Serve while the crema is still gold.
caffe-crema.proTip: A long pull, not an americano.

americano-misto.description: Americano with a little steamed milk. Lighter than a latte, rounder than black.
method: Hot water in a warm 200–220 ml cup.
Pull 30–35 ml espresso into the water.
Milk to 60–65°C, light texture, not a cap of foam.
A small pour on the americano. Stir once if you need to.
Serve hot.
americano-misto.proTip: Keep the milk small. You are softening an americano, not building a latte.

guest-espresso.description: The house espresso service, with the guest lot in the basket. Origin and roast in a small cup.
method: Warm a small cup.
Even puck. Pull 30–35 ml.
Serve at once, with one short note on the coffee.
One tasting cue. Not a lecture.
guest-espresso.proTip: Not a new build. The lot is the story.
guest-espresso.serve: 50–70 ml demitasse. Water beside it if you like.

drip-coffee.description: Automatic drip. Bright acidity, clear sweetness, a smooth body.
method: Grind on demand to drip. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Start the brewer. The bed should wet evenly, not tunnel down one side.
Target 4:00–6:00. Too fast is thin; too slow is dry.
Time is a check. Taste, then change grind or dose.
Serve fresh. Do not hold past the house window.
drip-coffee.proTip: Automatic drip still needs dial-in; if the machine is fixed, grind and dose are your control points.
drip-coffee.serve: 250–300 ml preheated mug; serve hot, offer refills only while the batch is in window.

filter-coffee.description: Paper filter. A clean cup, bright acidity, a tea-like finish when grind and drawdown line up.
method: Grind on demand to filter. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Bloom 30–45 seconds until the bed is wet.
Pour in pulses. Keep the bed level.
Target 2:45–4:00 for a 250–320 ml cup.
Serve at once, while the aroma is clean.
filter-coffee.proTip: Drawdown is a diagnostic, not a trophy: use it with taste to decide whether to grind finer, coarser or pour calmer.
filter-coffee.serve: 250–300 ml into a warm cup; serve while the aromatics are fresh.

batch-brew.description: Batch filter for volume. Same ratio, even extraction, a bright filter cup at café scale.
method: Grind on demand to batch-filter. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Start the batch. The spray should wet the bed evenly in the first minute.
Target 4:00–6:00. Change grind before you change the ratio.
Serve within the house window. Discard coffee that tastes hollow or baked.
batch-brew.proTip: Batch brew earns trust through repeatability: log dose, yield, grind, brew time and discard time every service.
batch-brew.serve: 250–300 ml preheated mug; serve hot within your posted batch window.

pour-over-coffee.description: Manual filter. Clear aromatics, bright acidity, a light body when the pour is controlled.
method: Grind on demand to pour-over. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Bloom 30–45 seconds.
Pour in calm pulses or a steady spiral. Keep the bed level.
Target 2:45–3:45 for a 250–320 ml cup.
Serve at once. Do not hold the brew.
pour-over-coffee.proTip: A premium pour-over should taste cleaner because it is controlled, not because it is slower for theatre.
pour-over-coffee.serve: 250–320 ml carafe into a warm 200–260 ml cup; serve fresh.

chemex.description: Chemex — exceptional clarity, floral highs, a clean sweet finish. Thicker paper, slower drawdown.
method: Grind on demand to a medium-coarse Chemex grind. Preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Rinse the thick paper thoroughly.
Bloom 35–45 seconds. Pour in wide, calm spirals.
Target 4:00–5:30. Swirl the carafe.
Serve while the clarity is still high.
chemex.proTip: Chemex is a clarity brewer; rushed pours or an under-rinsed filter make a premium coffee taste papery and flat.
chemex.serve: 300–320 ml carafe into a preheated 260 ml cup; first pour at the bar.

aeropress.description: Immersion and a short press. Full body, low bitterness, a bright cup.
method: Grind on demand to AeroPress. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Add water. Stir only to wet the grounds. Steep 1:30–2:30.
Press steadily 20–30 seconds. Do not force the plunger.
Serve at once. Bypass with water only if the house recipe is a longer cup.
aeropress.proTip: AeroPress is fast immersion: time controls sweetness, pressure controls texture; do not turn it into a forced espresso substitute.
aeropress.serve: 250–280 ml into a warm cup; drink while aroma still rises from the surface.

french-press.description: Full immersion. Heavy body, rustic texture, oils in the cup — not trapped in paper.
method: Grind on demand to a coarse press grind. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Water on. Saturate the grounds. Steep 4:00.
Break the crust. Press slowly.
Decant at once. The pot is not a holding vessel.
french-press.proTip: French press is not a holding vessel; the brew must leave the grounds when the extraction window is reached.
french-press.serve: 280–300 ml preheated mug; serve hot, not scorching.

moka-pot.description: Stovetop pressure. Dense, espresso-like intensity without the machine. A small Italian cup.
method: Grind on demand to moka. Hot water in the base, to the valve. Dose the basket even. Do not tamp.
Medium heat. The coffee should flow steadily, not spurt.
About 3:00–5:00 from heat-on. Off the heat before the bitter sputter.
Serve at once. Moka is pressure-assisted coffee, not espresso.
moka-pot.proTip: Moka quality depends on stopping before the bitter sputter; the pot is pressure-assisted, not espresso.
moka-pot.serve: 150–180 ml warm cup; drink while steam still rises.

flash-chilled-coffee.description: Hot filter, flash-chilled over ice. Japanese-style clarity, cold in the glass.
flash-chilled-coffee.yield: 17 g coffee, 250 ml water, over ice
method: Grind on demand to filter. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
A planned hot-water-to-ice split. Brew the stronger hot filter directly over measured hard ice.
Target 2:45–3:45 hot drawdown. Swirl once so the ice melts and chills the brew.
Pour over fresh hard ice if needed. Serve at once.
flash-chilled-coffee.proTip: Flash-chilled coffee is the fast service alternative to cold brew: hot extraction, measured ice and immediate chill, not shaken espresso.
flash-chilled-coffee.serve: 300–350 ml glass over full ice; serve cold, at once.

iced-filter-coffee.description: Filter over ice. Bright, clean, refreshing — brew strong so dilution stays in control.
iced-filter-coffee.yield: 17 g coffee, 250 ml water, over ice
method: Grind on demand to filter. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Brew a stronger hot filter directly over measured hard ice. Target 2:45–3:45.
Do not pour warm coffee over weak service ice.
Serve cold, over hard ice.
iced-filter-coffee.proTip: Iced filter should be designed around dilution; warm brewed coffee over random ice is not a recipe.
iced-filter-coffee.serve: 300–350 ml glass over full ice; straw optional.

cold-brew-coffee.description: A 12–18 hour cold steep. Low acid, round sweetness, cocoa and nut in the cup.
method: Grind on demand, coarse. Coffee and cold water, fully wet. Cover. Steep cold 12–18 hours.
Filter clean. No grit in the glass.
A house rapid extraction is fine if it tastes against the long steep.
Dilute to drinking strength. Hard ice, or neat if they want it stronger.
cold-brew-coffee.proTip: Fast cold brew is a production method, not a shortcut in standards: validate rapid extraction by taste, clarity, strength and filtration before selling it.
cold-brew-coffee.serve: 350–400 ml tall glass over full ice; straw optional.

nitro-cold-brew.description: Cold brew with nitrogen. Cascading crema, a creamy mouthfeel, extra sweetness without milk.
method: Grind on demand, coarse. Cold brew base: 12–18 hours, or a house rapid extraction tasted against the long steep.
Filter carefully. No fines in the keg.
Chill fully. Charge or pour through nitro until the cascade and head appear.
Serve cold. Ice only if the tap is not cold enough.
nitro-cold-brew.proTip: Let the cascade settle, then serve in a tall glass so guests see the texture before the first sip.
nitro-cold-brew.serve: 350–400 ml tall glass; serve cold with the nitrogen head intact.

cold-brew-tonic.description: Cold brew over tonic and ice. Bitter sparkle, low acid, a tall cup without espresso heat.
method: A clean cold-brew base: 12–18 hours, or a house rapid extraction tasted against the long steep.
Hard ice. Chilled tonic first.
Cold brew slowly over the tonic.
Serve before the bubbles fade.
cold-brew-tonic.proTip: Pick one tonic label for the house—changing brands changes bitterness more than a grind tick.
cold-brew-tonic.serve: 300–360 ml Collins over full ice; serve with a tall straw for one stir.

barrel-aged-cold-brew.description: Cold brew from a named barrel-aged lot. Oak and spirit-barrel aroma — not woody bitterness.
method: Verified barrel-aged beans. Grind on demand, coarse. Cold water, fully wet. Steep 12–18 hours.
Filter clean. Dilute to drinking strength.
A house rapid extraction is fine if it tastes against the long steep.
Hard ice, or neat. The value is aroma, not wood.
barrel-aged-cold-brew.proTip: Keep this recipe only as a seasonal premium item with a named barrel-aged lot or documented oak process; otherwise replace it with standard cold brew.
barrel-aged-cold-brew.serve: 350–400 ml tall glass over full ice; straw optional.

reserve-pour-over.description: Reserve single-origin pour-over. The lot, the time, and one tasting cue.
method: Name the lot first: origin, process where you know it, roast rest, one tasting note.
Grind on demand to the dialled reserve grind. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Bloom 30–45 seconds. Calm, repeatable pulses. Keep the bed level.
Target 2:45–3:45 for a 300–320 ml cup.
Small carafe, warm cup, one cue. Do not hold it.
reserve-pour-over.proTip: Reserve pour-over only earns its menu space when the guest can taste and understand the lot: name it, dial it, time it and serve it immediately.
reserve-pour-over.serve: 300–320 ml small carafe into a warm cup; serve with lot name, origin/process cue and expected tasting notes.

espresso-macchiato.description: Espresso marked with a small spoon of foam. Coffee first. Not a mini cappuccino.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml into a small warm cup.
While the shot runs, steam a little milk. You need the foam, not a pour.
1–2 spoons of glossy foam through the crema.
Do not fill it with liquid milk. Serve at once.
espresso-macchiato.proTip: Well-textured dairy or plant-based foam from a tested product should be fine, glossy and stable: microbubbles hold longer, look smoother and give a creamier mouthfeel than.
espresso-macchiato.serve: 50–70 ml warm espresso cup; visible foam mark on the crema.

cortado.description: Espresso cut with near-equal warm milk. Coffee-forward, short, smooth.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C with only light microfoam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the coffee. Serve at once.
cortado.proTip: Cortado means cut: the milk softens espresso without turning it into a piccolo or flat white.
cortado.serve: 120–150 ml warm glass or cup; serve immediately, at once.

piccolo-latte.description: A mini latte. A short espresso base, 70–90 ml silky milk, in a small glass.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull a short espresso, about 20–25 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into glossy, pourable microfoam — not a dry cap.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour like a small latte. Serve at once, in a 90–110 ml glass.
piccolo-latte.proTip: Piccolo is not just another word for cortado: use a shorter coffee base and more latte-like microfoam.
piccolo-latte.serve: 90–110 ml warm glass; serve immediately, at once.

gibraltar.description: Cortado balance in a Gibraltar glass. Tight ratio, San Francisco bar classic.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C with only light microfoam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the coffee. Serve at once.
gibraltar.proTip: The glass is the service. In a larger cup, it is a cortado — call it that.
gibraltar.serve: 130–150 ml preheated Gibraltar glass; serve immediately, at once.

flat-white.description: Tighter than a latte. A double espresso, 90–110 ml velvet microfoam, a 150–180 ml cup.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 60–70 ml — a double.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C with very little air: glossy, pourable microfoam, not cappuccino foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the coffee. Serve at once.
flat-white.proTip: A flat white fails when the milk becomes too airy; keep it tight and polished.
flat-white.serve: 150–180 ml warm cup; serve immediately while the microfoam is glossy.

cappuccino.description: Espresso, warm milk, dense microfoam. Aroma through the foam, sweetness in the milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into dense, glossy cappuccino foam. Keep a cap, not peaks.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour through the espresso. Finish with a clear foam cap. Do not stir. Serve at once.
cappuccino.proTip: Foam that stands in peaks belongs on a pie, not in this cup—velvet cap, not meringue.
cappuccino.serve: 160–200 ml warm cup; guest should smell coffee through the foam on the first lift.

latte.description: Espresso on steamed milk, a thin microfoam lid. Comfort in the cup.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into glossy, pourable microfoam — not a dry cap.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the coffee. Serve at once.
latte.proTip: If the drink tastes sweet but empty, fix the espresso before you reach for syrup—the milk is already doing sweetness work.
latte.serve: 280–320 ml cup or glass; hot through the last third.

latte-macchiato.description: Steamed milk marked with espresso. Milk first. A stain on top.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into glossy, pourable microfoam — not a dry cap.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Milk in a tall glass first, a soft foam layer on top.
Pull 30–35 ml. Pour slowly through the milk so the mark stays.
Serve at once.
latte-macchiato.proTip: Latte macchiato is milk marked with coffee, not the small foam-dolloped espresso macchiato.
latte-macchiato.serve: 280–320 ml glass; guest sees the mark before the first sip.

mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. No chocolate left on the bottom.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; serve while the surface still shines.

espresso-con-panna.description: Espresso crowned with softly whipped cream. Coffee-forward, barely sweet.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Lightly whip cold cream until it is soft and pourable, not stiff.
Float the cream over the back of a spoon.
Serve at once — hot coffee, cool cream.
espresso-con-panna.proTip: Soft cream is the point: stiff peaks block aroma, while softly whipped cream lets the espresso come through.
espresso-con-panna.serve: 50–70 ml demitasse; hot espresso with a soft cool cream cap.

breve-latte.description: Espresso with steamed half-and-half. Richer than a whole-milk latte.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Half-and-half to 60–65°C. Stretch less than milk — the cream thickens quickly.
Pour into the espresso. Serve at once.
breve-latte.proTip: Half-and-half thickens quickly. Stretch less than milk, and keep 60–65°C.
breve-latte.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

cafe-au-lait.description: Filter coffee and scalded milk, about equal parts. A French breakfast cup — not espresso.
method: Grind on demand to filter. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Brew 220 ml fresh filter or batch coffee.
Milk to 60–65°C, light texture. Not cappuccino foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Coffee and milk in roughly equal parts, into a large warm cup. Serve hot.
cafe-au-lait.proTip: Scalded milk is the texture—if you steam to cappuccino foam, you are making something else.
cafe-au-lait.serve: 400–450 ml preheated bowl or cup; equal coffee and milk by volume.

galao.description: Portuguese tall glass. Espresso lengthened with foamed milk — more than a cortado, less than a latte.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C with only light microfoam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the coffee. Serve at once.
galao.proTip: Galão sits between cortado and cappuccino—when in doubt, less milk than a latte, more foam than a flat white.
galao.serve: 200–240 ml tall glass; hand warm with foam still holding shape.

cafe-con-leche.description: Espresso folded through steamed milk. A Spanish morning cup, without latte volume.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into glossy, pourable microfoam — not a dry cap.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the coffee. Serve at once.
cafe-con-leche.proTip: Café con leche is not a flavoured latte—let coffee and milk do the work without syrup.
cafe-con-leche.serve: 200–240 ml warm cup; hot through the last sip.

dirty-coffee.description: Cold milk base with hot fresh espresso poured on top.
method: Hard ice in a chilled glass.
Cold whole milk on the ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Pour the shot last, directly over the ice.
Serve at once.
dirty-coffee.proTip: Temperature contrast is the recipe—warm milk kills the layer before the guest sees it.
dirty-coffee.serve: 280–320 ml glass; cold milk, hot espresso crown, no pass time.

dry-cappuccino.description: A cappuccino with a lighter body and a more pronounced dry foam cap.
dry-cappuccino.yield: 30–35 ml espresso + milk and dry foam
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into fine, dry foam — structured, not coarse.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour through the espresso. Finish with the cap. Do not stir. Serve at once.
dry-cappuccino.proTip: Dry cappuccino is not a cup of foam.
dry-cappuccino.serve: 160–200 ml cappuccino cup; pronounced foam cap with clear espresso aroma.

oat-latte.description: A latte on barista oat milk. Creamy, lightly cereal-sweet, dairy-free.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Barista oat milk to 60–65°C, smooth and glossy. Less air than dairy.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour into the espresso. Serve at once.
oat-latte.proTip: Oat milk rewards less air and slightly lower heat.
oat-latte.serve: Serve in a 240–300 ml cup or glass; smooth, integrated and not overheated.

spanish-latte.description: Espresso, condensed milk, steamed milk. Caramel-edged, still coffee-forward.
spanish-latte.yield: 30–35 ml espresso + condensed milk + steamed milk
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Condensed milk into the hot shot. Stir until even.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into glossy, pourable microfoam — not a dry cap.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour. Serve at once.
spanish-latte.proTip: Condensed milk is the sweetener—cut it before you add syrup or the cup turns candy.
spanish-latte.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

affogato.description: Espresso poured over cold gelato. Instant cooling, bitter-sweet cream.
ingredients: Vanilla gelato, 80–160 g; one large scoop or two smaller scoops depending on glass size
method: Cold gelato in a chilled bowl or glass — one large scoop, or two smaller.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. A strong moka will stand in.
Pour at once, from the spouts if you can, onto the gelato.
Spoon. Serve while the surface is just beginning to melt.
affogato.proTip: Affogato improves when the hot espresso meets the frozen gelato instantly: faster cooling preserves more espresso aroma, keeps the gelato texture cleaner and creates a smoother.
affogato.serve: Chilled 120–160 ml bowl or glass; one large scoop or two smaller scoops; spoon on the saucer, napkin ready.

bicerin.description: Hot chocolate, espresso, softly whipped cream. Three layers. No steamed milk.
method: Melt the dark chocolate until smooth and pourable. Into the heatproof glass.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Pour over the back of a spoon, or down the glass, to keep a layer.
Soft, glossy cream — not stiff. Spoon on top.
Do not stir. Serve at once.
bicerin.proTip: Use real dark chocolate pieces/callets as the default base for Bicerin; prepare the chocolate base separately until smooth and glossy before layering espresso and the soft.
bicerin.serve: 150–180 ml heatproof glass; three visible tones, Serve immediately.

white-chocolate-mocha.description: White chocolate and espresso, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
White chocolate in the cup. A splash of hot milk if it needs loosening. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
white-chocolate-mocha.proTip: White chocolate is sweet and delicate: use a little hot milk only if needed to loosen it, then pour the full fresh espresso over it so the chocolate and coffee integrate cleanly.
white-chocolate-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; serve while the surface still shines.

caramel-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. Caramel syrup in. Stir before the milk.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
caramel-mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
caramel-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

salted-caramel-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.
ingredients: Salted caramel syrup (sweetened caramel syrup with salt), 12 ml
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. Salted caramel syrup in. Taste before you add salt.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
salted-caramel-mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
salted-caramel-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; serve hot and fresh, never held until dull.

dark-chocolate-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Extra dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. Nothing left on the bottom.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
dark-chocolate-mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
dark-chocolate-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; serve while the surface still shines.

gianduja-latte.description: Gianduja and espresso, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Gianduja paste in a warm cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until smooth and glossy.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into glossy, pourable microfoam — not a dry cap.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
gianduja-latte.proTip: If it tastes too sweet, use slightly less gianduja paste next time.
gianduja-latte.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

chocolate-cappuccino.description: Real dark chocolate pieces/callets and fresh espresso under dense cappuccino foam.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C into dense, glossy cappuccino foam. Keep a cap, not peaks.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour through the chocolate base. Cap with foam. Do not stir. Serve at once.
chocolate-cappuccino.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
chocolate-cappuccino.serve: 160–200 ml warm cup; guest should smell coffee through foam on the first lift.

hot-chocolate.description: Milk chocolate, whole milk, enough cocoa depth to feel crafted — not thin, not powdered.
method: Chocolate in a pan. A small splash of milk. Warm, whisk, until a glossy paste.
The rest of the milk. Heat to 60–70°C. Whisk until smooth. Do not boil.
Taste before you add sugar.
Warm cup. Serve before a skin forms.
hot-chocolate.proTip: Start with real chocolate and a small milk splash.
hot-chocolate.serve: Serve in a 250–300 ml warm cup; add thin milk foam only when specified, never a heavy dry cap.

marzipan-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. Almond syrup in.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
marzipan-mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
marzipan-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

tiramisu-coffee.description: Espresso, mascarpone-style cream, cocoa dust. Dessert cues — not a tiramisu slab.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Lightly whip cold cream until soft and pourable.
Float the cream over the back of a spoon.
A light cocoa dust. Serve at once.
tiramisu-coffee.proTip: Use cocoa as a light aromatic dusting only; the drink should read as coffee plus soft cream, not as a chocolate-base mocha.
tiramisu-coffee.serve: 140–160 ml demitasse or dessert cup; spoon on saucer, napkin folded small.

viennese-coffee.description: Hot coffee or espresso, softly whipped cream, a light cocoa finish.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew.
Lightly whip cold cream until soft and pourable.
Float the cream over the back of a spoon.
A light cocoa dust. Serve at once.
viennese-coffee.proTip: Use cocoa as a light aromatic dusting only; too much makes the first sip dry and bitter.
viennese-coffee.serve: 150–180 ml warm handled cup; hot coffee base with a soft cream cap.

orange-chocolate-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. A restrained orange syrup. Chocolate leads.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
orange-chocolate-mocha.proTip: Keep this version chocolate-led: if the orange tastes like soft drink, reduce syrup before changing the chocolate dose.
orange-chocolate-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

iced-americano.description: Fresh espresso lengthened with cold water over ice.
method: Hard ice in a chilled glass.
Cold filtered water on the ice, room for the shot.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Pour the shot last, directly over the ice.
Serve at once.
iced-americano.proTip: Build over cold water and hard ice; shaking turns an iced americano into a different drink.
iced-americano.serve: 280–320 ml glass over full ice; serve cold.

iced-red-eye.description: Cold batch coffee crowned with fresh espresso over ice.
method: Chill the brew first.
Hard ice. Cold filter or batch coffee in the glass.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Pour last, over the cold brew.
Serve at once.
iced-red-eye.proTip: Keep the batch coffee cold and clean; the espresso should add lift, not hide stale brewed coffee.
iced-red-eye.serve: 320–360 ml glass over full ice; cold through the last sip.

quad-on-ice.description: Four fresh espresso shots over ice.
method: Hard ice in a small chilled glass.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Four shots, about 120–140 ml in total. Each puck even.
Pour last, directly over the ice. Do not shake.
Serve at once.
quad-on-ice.proTip: Use enough hard ice and serve fast; four shots over weak ice become harsh and diluted.
quad-on-ice.serve: 120–160 ml glass over ice; serve cold within seconds of the last pour.

iced-cortado.description: Fresh espresso cut with cold milk over ice.
method: Hard ice in a chilled glass.
Cold whole milk on the ice — keep the ratio short.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Pour the shot last, directly over the ice.
Serve at once.
iced-cortado.proTip: Iced cortado is a ratio drink—too much milk and you are serving an iced latte in a small glass.
iced-cortado.serve: 120–150 ml glass over ice; serve cold.

iced-latte.description: Cold milk and a fresh espresso over ice.
method: Hard ice in a chilled glass.
Cold whole milk on the ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Pour the shot last, directly over the ice.
Serve at once.
iced-latte.proTip: Ice dilution calls for a tighter fresh espresso — taste beats the clock if the cup is clean.
iced-latte.serve: 280–320 ml glass over full ice; serve cold, at once.

iced-flat-white.description: Two fresh espressos over cold milk and ice.
method: Hard ice in a chilled glass. Cold whole milk on the ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Two shots, 30–35 ml each.
Pour last, directly over the ice.
Serve at once.
iced-flat-white.proTip: Two shots on ice need a sweet dial-in—dilution punishes dull espresso faster than hot milk does.
iced-flat-white.serve: 200–240 ml glass over ice; cold through the last sip.

iced-mocha.description: Real dark chocolate pieces/callets and fresh espresso cooled with cold milk over ice.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. Cool briefly.
Hard ice. Cold milk. Stir until even.
Serve cold.
iced-mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
iced-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml glass over full ice; serve cold.

shakerato.description: Espresso shaken on ice with a touch of sugar.
method: Chill a small glass. Sugar in the shaker.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Into the shaker while it is fresh.
Hard ice. Shake hard 10–15 seconds.
Strain, no ice in the glass. Serve at once.
shakerato.proTip: Too little ice makes a thin drink; too much ice and a long shake strip the aromatics—use one full scoop, one hard shake.
shakerato.serve: Chilled 120–150 ml stem or small coupe; foam should hold a spoon for a moment.

freddo-espresso.description: A Greek-style iced espresso shaken cold until it has a light coffee foam and a clean, strong finish..
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Hard ice in a shaker. Shake hard 10–15 seconds until cold and lightly foamy.
Strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice.
Serve while the foam still sits.
freddo-espresso.proTip: Use fresh hard ice for the shake, then fresh ice in the glass so the drink stays strong instead of watery.
freddo-espresso.serve: 120–150 ml chilled glass; foam should hold a line on the rim.

freddo-cappuccino.description: A Greek-style iced espresso topped with a light cold milk foam cap. The coffee stays chilled and visible underneath..
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Shake or stir with hard ice until cold. Into a chilled glass with fresh ice.
Cold milk, frothed separately, until light glossy cold foam.
Spoon the foam on top. The coffee stays visible.
Do not stir unless they want it mixed. Serve at once.
freddo-cappuccino.serve: 200–240 ml glass over ice; cold foam cap, coffee base visible below.

cold-foam-cappuccino.description: Iced espresso finished with a separate cold milk foam cap.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Shake or stir with hard ice until cold. Into a chilled glass with fresh ice.
Cold milk, frothed separately, until light glossy cold foam.
Spoon the foam on top. The coffee stays visible.
Do not stir unless they want it mixed. Serve at once.
cold-foam-cappuccino.serve: 160–200 ml glass or cup; foam cap firm, coffee base aromatic.

blended-coffee-frappe.description: Fresh espresso blended with milk and ice.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly.
Espresso, cold milk, sugar, hard ice in the blender.
Blend until cold, foamy and pourable. Stop before it turns watery.
Chilled glass. Serve at once.
blended-coffee-frappe.proTip: Ice is the body—too little ice makes a thin shake, too much and coffee flavour washes out.
blended-coffee-frappe.serve: 350–400 ml chilled glass; thick enough to hold a straw upright for a moment.

frappe-coffee.description: Shaken or blended iced coffee with foam.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly.
Espresso, a little cold milk, sugar, hard ice. Shake or blend until foamy.
Tall glass. Serve before the foam collapses.
frappe-coffee.proTip: Vigorous shake beats gentle stir—frappé foam is the texture, not a garnish.
frappe-coffee.serve: 300–350 ml tall glass; foam cap high, drink cold throughout.

granita.description: Frozen coffee, scraped to crystals. Cold, sweet-edged, between dessert and iced coffee.
granita.yield: Strong brew, 40 g sugar, frozen and scraped
method: Grind on demand to filter. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
A strong brew. Dissolve the sugar while it is hot.
Shallow tray. Freeze. Scrape with a fork every 30–45 minutes.
Serve when it is loose, icy, spoonable.
granita.proTip: Use a shallow tray and scrape regularly; one solid frozen block gives coarse ice, not granita.
granita.serve: 150–200 ml chilled bowl or glass; spoon on the side.

espresso-tonic.description: Tonic’s bitterness and fine bubbles lift fresh espresso oils.
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly over ice so it does not flatten the bubbles.
Tonic in the glass.
Sparkling mixer down the ice, slowly.
Coffee last, gently over the top. Stir once only if you need to. Serve while it sparkles.
espresso-tonic.proTip: Never shake tonic and espresso together; you lose both bubbles and aroma.
espresso-tonic.serve: 300–360 ml Collins; serve with a tall straw so guests can stir once before the last sip.

espresso-lemonade.description: Fresh lemonade and fresh espresso over ice.
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly over ice so it does not flatten the bubbles.
Lemonade in the glass.
Sparkling mixer down the ice, slowly.
Coffee last, gently over the top. Stir once only if you need to. Serve while it sparkles.
espresso-lemonade.proTip: Sweet lemonade plus espresso both carry acid—taste the lemonade neat before you blame the shot for sharpness.
espresso-lemonade.serve: 300–350 ml Collins over full ice; serve cold with a tall straw.

espresso-cola.description: Cola and fresh espresso over ice.
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly over ice so it does not flatten the bubbles.
Cola in the glass.
Sparkling mixer down the ice, slowly.
Coffee last, gently over the top. Stir once only if you need to. Serve while it sparkles.
espresso-cola.proTip: Espresso last, cola cold—warm cola reads flat and makes the shot taste ashy.
espresso-cola.serve: 300–350 ml highball over full ice; straw on the side.

yuzu-espresso-tonic.description: Yuzu, tonic, and fresh espresso over ice.
ingredients: Yuzu syrup (sweetened yuzu citrus syrup), 10 ml
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly over ice so it does not flatten the bubbles.
Yuzu syrup in first. Then tonic.
Sparkling mixer down the ice, slowly.
Coffee last, gently over the top. Stir once only if you need to. Serve while it sparkles.
yuzu-espresso-tonic.proTip: Yuzu is perfume, not volume—cut syrup before you dilute the coffee further.
yuzu-espresso-tonic.serve: 300–360 ml Collins over full ice; serve with a tall straw for one stir.

espresso-mojito.description: Mint, lime, soda, and fresh espresso over ice.
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly over ice so it does not flatten the bubbles.
Mint, lime and sugar syrup in first. Then soda.
Sparkling mixer down the ice, slowly.
Coffee last, gently over the top. Stir once only if you need to. Serve while it sparkles.
espresso-mojito.proTip: Mint and espresso both bring bitter—pull a sweet shot or the cup turns one-note sharp.
espresso-mojito.serve: 300–350 ml highball over full ice; straw for one stir at the table.

brown-sugar-shaken-espresso.description: Fresh espresso shaken with brown sugar syrup and ice.
ingredients: Brown sugar syrup (dissolved brown sugar syrup), 15 ml
method: Brown sugar syrup in the shaker.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml onto the syrup while it is hot, so the sugar dissolves.
Hard ice. Shake hard 10–15 seconds.
Chilled glass, fresh ice. Serve while the foam holds a line.
brown-sugar-shaken-espresso.proTip: Brown sugar must dissolve in the hot espresso before the shake; otherwise the last sip tastes sweet and gritty.
brown-sugar-shaken-espresso.serve: 200–250 ml chilled glass; foam should hold a line on the rim.

orange-coffee-spritz.description: Cold brew, orange, and soda in a coffee spritz.
orange-coffee-spritz.yield: Coffee, 36 g · Water, 120 ml · Soda water, 120 ml
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Prepared cold brew, fully chilled.
Orange syrup in first.
Soda down the ice, slowly.
Cold brew last, gently. Serve while it sparkles.
orange-coffee-spritz.proTip: Orange should lift the cold coffee like peel oil, not turn it into soft drink; keep syrup modest, use hard ice and pour the coffee gently so the top still smells like coffee.
orange-coffee-spritz.serve: 280–320 ml stem or highball; cold stem keeps spritz honest in the hand.

coconut-cold-brew.description: Cold brew with coconut over ice.
coconut-cold-brew.yield: Coffee, 72 g · Water, 240 ml · Coconut milk (drinkable chilled coconut milk, not canned cooking cream unless specified), 60 ml
ingredients: Coconut milk (drinkable chilled coconut milk, not canned cooking cream unless specified), 60 ml
method: Cold brew base: coarse grind, 12–18 hours, or a house rapid extraction tasted against the long steep.
Filter, chill, dilute to drinking strength.
Hard ice. Chilled coconut milk. Coffee still leads.
Serve before the ice softens or the coconut separates.
coconut-cold-brew.proTip: Carton coconut varies in sweetness batch to batch—taste every new case before you line it up for rush.
coconut-cold-brew.serve: 350–400 ml tall glass over full ice; straw optional.

sparkling-cascara.description: Cascara tea and soda over ice.
sparkling-cascara.yield: Cascara (dried coffee cherry husk for tea/infusion), 12 g · Water, 200 ml · Soda water, 100 ml
ingredients: Cascara (dried coffee cherry husk for tea/infusion), 12 g
method: Steep cascara in hot water. Chill the infusion fully.
Hard ice in a chilled glass.
Soda down the ice, slowly.
Serve while it sparkles.
sparkling-cascara.proTip: Cascara punishes over-steep—woody tea reads like bark; cut time before you add sugar.
sparkling-cascara.serve: 280–320 ml stem or highball over ice; serve cold.

cascara-spritz.description: Cascara, citrus, and sparkling water in an aperitivo spritz.
cascara-spritz.yield: Cascara (dried coffee cherry husk for tea/infusion), 12 g · Water, 160 ml · Soda water, 120 ml
ingredients: Cascara (dried coffee cherry husk for tea/infusion), 12 g
method: Steep cascara in hot water. Chill the infusion fully.
Hard ice. Orange syrup in first.
Soda down the ice, slowly.
Serve while it sparkles.
cascara-spritz.proTip: Orange lifts cascara—when the first sip is only sweet, cut syrup before you weaken the tea.
cascara-spritz.serve: 280–320 ml stem or highball; cold stem keeps spritz honest in the hand.

blackberry-coffee-soda.description: Cold coffee, soda and blackberry over ice.
blackberry-coffee-soda.yield: Coffee, 36 g · Water, 120 ml · Soda water, 120 ml
method: Prepared cold brew, fully chilled.
Hard ice. Blackberry syrup in first.
Soda down the ice, slowly.
Cold brew last, gently. Serve while it sparkles.
blackberry-coffee-soda.proTip: Blackberry syrup reads sticky fast once carbonation opens the aroma; keep the cold coffee clean, add soda gently and cut syrup before adding more coffee if the first sip turns.
blackberry-coffee-soda.serve: 280–320 ml stem or highball; cold stem keeps spritz honest in the hand.

caffe-corretto.description: Espresso corrected with grappa. Italian after-dinner. Hot coffee, spirit in the cup.
method: Warm the demitasse, then empty it.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Grappa in the warm cup.
Pull 30–35 ml into the spirit.
Serve at once.
caffe-corretto.proTip: Grappa quality shows in three sips—cheap spirit makes even good espresso taste harsh.
caffe-corretto.serve: 50–70 ml warm demitasse plus 30 ml grappa; serve immediately.

carajillo.description: Hot fresh espresso with warm brandy.
method: Warm a heatproof glass, then empty it.
Brandy in.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml into the spirit.
Serve at once.
carajillo.proTip: Warm brandy, hot espresso, immediate handoff—delay turns aroma flat.
carajillo.serve: 80–100 ml heatproof glass; hot enough to steam gently.

irish-coffee.description: Hot coffee, Irish whiskey, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Irish whiskey in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
irish-coffee.proTip: Float the cream softly; the guest should drink through it, not stir it in.
irish-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

gaelic-coffee.description: Hot coffee, Scotch whisky, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Scotch whisky in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
gaelic-coffee.proTip: Float the cream softly; the guest should drink through it, not stir it in.
gaelic-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

kentucky-coffee.description: Hot coffee, bourbon, brown sugar, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Bourbon in. Brown sugar, not white.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
kentucky-coffee.proTip: Brown sugar reads rounder than white here—dissolve fully before bourbon goes in.
kentucky-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

jamaican-coffee.description: Hot coffee, dark rum, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Dark rum in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
jamaican-coffee.proTip: Dark rum wants a sweet, clean shot—harsh espresso and rum fight instead of marry.
jamaican-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

calypso-coffee.description: Hot coffee, white rum, coconut liqueur, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
White rum and coconut liqueur in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
calypso-coffee.proTip: Coconut liqueur punishes heavy hands—taste before you line up a double.
calypso-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

mexican-coffee.description: Hot coffee, tequila, coffee liqueur, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Tequila and coffee liqueur in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
mexican-coffee.proTip: Coffee liqueur adds sweetness—dissolve sugar first and taste before a second spoon.
mexican-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

spanish-coffee.description: Hot coffee, dark rum, coffee liqueur, triple sec, and floated cream.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Dark rum, coffee liqueur and triple sec in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
spanish-coffee.proTip: Flaming is theatre, not flavour—if safety says no flame, the unflamed build still tastes right.
spanish-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

pharisaer.description: German coffee with rum under a floated cream cap.

toasted-marshmallow-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.

Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy. Marshmallow syrup in.

Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.

toasted-marshmallow-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

cranberry-white-mocha.description: White chocolate and espresso, folded through steamed milk.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
White chocolate in the cup. Loosen with a splash of hot milk if needed. Pour the shot over. Cranberry syrup in.
While the shot runs, steam milk to 60–65°C until glossy and creamy, not dry foam.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
cranberry-white-mocha.proTip: White chocolate is sweet and delicate: use a little hot milk only if needed to loosen it, then pour the full fresh espresso over it so the chocolate and coffee integrate cleanly.
cranberry-white-mocha.serve: 280–320 ml warm cup; hot through the last third.

spring-honey-flat-white.description: Honey syrup and one double espresso (60–70 ml).

Honey syrup into the hot shot. Stir until even.

90–110 ml milk into a 150–180 ml cup. Serve at once.
spring-honey-flat-white.proTip: Spring honey reads louder than winter maple on a tight ratio—start at half pump and taste.
spring-honey-flat-white.serve: 150–180 ml warm cup; serve immediately while the microfoam is glossy.

peter-s-velvet-ristretto.description: A short, dense espresso. Sweet, syrupy, Peter’s window for clarity and body.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 18–22 ml. Stop while sweetness is still leading.
Serve at once.
peter-s-velvet-ristretto.proTip: Do not chase volume. If it is sour or harsh, change grind — not water, not milk.
peter-s-velvet-ristretto.serve: 60 ml warm cup; no saucer clutter—let the demitasse read as the whole gesture.

peter-s-oat-cortado.description: A compact oat-milk coffee with high espresso clarity.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Oat milk to 60–65°C, smooth and glossy. Stop before it cooks.
No steam wand: warm the milk to 60–65°C, froth 10–20 seconds, tap, swirl and pour while glossy.
Short pour. Cortado height, not latte height. Serve at once.
peter-s-oat-cortado.proTip: Oat turns bitter when the milk passes about 72°C (162°F)—stop the steam while the jug reads about 65°C (149°F) in the hand.
peter-s-oat-cortado.serve: 120 ml preheated glass; cortado height, not latte height.

hernou-reserve-mocha.description: Espresso and dark chocolate, folded through steamed milk.

Pour the milk into the chocolate base. Serve at once.
hernou-reserve-mocha.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
hernou-reserve-mocha.serve: 220 ml warm cup; serve hot, not tongue-scalding.

peter-s-espresso-tonic.description: Bright espresso over tonic with citrus lift and clean bitterness.
method: Chill the glass. Hard ice.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml. Cool briefly over ice so it does not flatten the bubbles.
Tonic in the glass.
Sparkling mixer down the ice, slowly.
Coffee last, gently over the top. Stir once only if you need to. Serve while it sparkles.
peter-s-espresso-tonic.proTip: Never shake tonic and espresso together.
peter-s-espresso-tonic.serve: 300 ml glass, full ice; straw on the side so guests can stir once before the last third.

peter-s-affogato-classico.description: Fresh espresso poured immediately over one scoop, or more, of vanilla gelato; Peter’s tableside classic with instant cooling and clean bitter-sweet cream.
ingredients: Vanilla gelato, 80–160 g; one large scoop or two smaller scoops depending on glass size
method: Vanilla gelato in a chilled dessert glass.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Pour at once onto the gelato — from the spouts if you can.
Spoon and napkin. Serve while the first melt is still creamy.
peter-s-affogato-classico.proTip: The theatre is the pour, but the quality is speed: espresso should hit the frozen gelato immediately, ideally direct from the espresso spouts/portafilter or moka pot, so aroma.
peter-s-affogato-classico.serve: 160 ml dessert glass; one large scoop or two smaller scoops; spoon and napkin, no side clutter.

peter-s-irish-coffee.description: Warm coffee, whiskey and cream with a clean layered finish.
method: Warm the glass, then empty it.
Irish whiskey in.
Sugar in. A splash of hot coffee. Stir until smooth.
Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml, or a fresh hot brew. Pour into the glass.
Softly whipped cream, floated. Do not stir it in. Serve at once.
peter-s-irish-coffee.proTip: Float the cream softly; the guest should drink through it, not stir it in.
peter-s-irish-coffee.serve: 240 ml handled glass; hot enough to steam gently, never lukewarm.

peter-s-chocolate-orange-espresso.description: Espresso, dark chocolate and orange aroma in a compact dessert coffee.
method: Grind on demand. Distribute, level the puck and tamp straight.
Pull 30–35 ml.
Dark chocolate in the cup. Pour the shot over. Stir until glossy.
Orange syrup in. No milk.
Serve at once, while it is warm and glossy.
peter-s-chocolate-orange-espresso.proTip: Real chocolate gives better body and finish than default powder.
peter-s-chocolate-orange-espresso.serve: 120–140 ml warm cup; demitasse saucer, no tall spoon.

peter-s-maple-flat-white.description: Flat white frame with maple warmth.

90–110 ml milk into a 150–180 ml cup. Serve at once.
peter-s-maple-flat-white.proTip: Pick one house rule—syrup before steam reads louder, syrup after steam reads rounder—and never switch mid-shift.
peter-s-maple-flat-white.serve: 150–180 ml warm cup; serve immediately while the microfoam is glossy.

peter-s-black-sesame-latte.description: Toasty black sesame with espresso and silky milk.

Pour. Serve at once.
peter-s-black-sesame-latte.proTip: Sesame clumps in cold milk—always pre-wet syrup before you touch steam.
peter-s-black-sesame-latte.serve: 240 ml warm cup; latte length, Peter’s flavour spine.

peter-s-reserve-pour-over.description: Peter’s reserve pour-over. The lot, a calm brew, one tasting cue.

Grind on demand to the dialled reserve grind. Rinse, preheat, dose even, level the bed.
Bloom 30–45 seconds. Calm pulses. Keep the bed level.
Target 2:45–3:45 for a 300–320 ml cup.
Small carafe. One cue. Not a lecture.
peter-s-reserve-pour-over.proTip: Peter’s reserve pour-over needs theatre with discipline: name the lot, brew it calmly, then give one concise tasting cue instead of a lecture.

peter-s-coffee-negroni.yield: Coffee, espresso dose · Gin, 25 ml · Campari, 25 ml

Gin, Campari, sweet vermouth.

Pull 30–35 ml last. Stir until cold. Strain.
Serve at once.

peter-s-coffee-negroni.serve: 200 ml rocks glass; cold enough to bite the lip, not so wet the ice is half melt.

peter-s-tiramisu-espresso.description: Espresso layered with mascarpone-style cream and cocoa.

Lightly whip cold cream until soft and pourable.

house-flat-white.serve: 150–180 ml warm cup; serve immediately while the microfoam is glossy.

cold-brew-spritz.description: Cold brew, soda, and citrus in a non-alcoholic coffee spritz.

Prepared cold brew, fully chilled.
Orange syrup in first.
Soda down the ice, slowly.
Cold brew last, gently. Serve while it sparkles.

Pour the shot last, directly over the ice.
Serve at once.

peter-s-chilly-choffy.description: A dense cold chocolate-coffee shake with dark ganache, coffee ice cubes, cold milk and vanilla ice cream..

Dark ganache with a splash of cold milk, until smooth.
Cold brew or chilled espresso, and coffee ice. Blend just to chill.

Serve at once.

Grand Marnier off the heat.
Soft cream, floated. Pomegranate and chocolate curls.
Serve at once.

peter-s-cuban-kiss.description: A warm chocolate-coffee cocktail with rum, cream and cacao warmth; served as a composed drink, not a boozy mocha shortcut..

Soft cream, floated. Serve hot. Do not boil after the rum is in.

pretty-in-pink.description: White chocolate, warm milk and beetroot.

Beetroot juice and the rest of the milk. Heat to 60–70°C until smooth and pink.

Serve before a skin forms.

peter-s-float-away.description: An oat-forward chocolate float with coffee depth, cool mint lift and a creamy finish..

Cold brew or chilled fresh espresso, 40 ml

Dark ganache with a splash of oat drink, until smooth.
Cold brew or chilled espresso, and mint. Blend or shake briefly.
Rest of the oat drink. Ice cream last, only until thick.
Mint. Serve cold.
peter-s-float-away.proTip: Cold chocolate drinks need texture control: blend until smooth, then stop before the body turns thin.
peter-s-float-away.serve: 250–300 ml chilled glass with spoon and straw.

chai-chocolatte.description: Dark chocolate melted into chai-infused milk.

Taste before you add sugar.
Warm cup. Serve before a skin forms.

sailing-off.description: Filter coffee, real dark chocolate and port.

Soft cream, floated. Cocoa nibs.

bed-of-roses.description: Dark chocolate, warm milk and restrained rose.
bed-of-roses.yield: Milk, 230 ml · Ground dark chocolate, 50 g · Rose syrup (sweetened rose syrup), 12 ml

Rest of the milk. Heat to 60–70°C until glossy.
Soft cream cap. Dark chocolate on top.
Serve before a skin forms. Rose is perfume, not volume.

orange-is-the-new-pink.description: Fluid dark chocolate ganache, sparkling rosé and orange blossom.

Orange-blossom water into the dark ganache until it loosens and looks glossy.
Ganache in the glass, below the sparkle.
Sparkling rosé down the side, slowly.
Edible flowers. Serve cold while it sparkles.
orange-is-the-new-pink.serve: Serve cold in a chilled coupe or cocktail glass with visible ganache and sparkling rosé layers.

straws-stripes.description: Strawberry, dark chocolate ganache and warm milk.
straws-stripes.yield: Fresh strawberries, 80 g · Liquid dark chocolate ganache, 50 ml · Milk, 200 ml
method: Dark ganache with a splash of milk, until smooth.
Strawberries and sugar into the base.
Rest of the milk, until glossy. Heat gently to 60–70°C if this is the hot serve.
Soft strawberry cream on top.
Serve at once, in a clear glass so the layers show.
straws-stripes.proTip: Cold chocolate drinks need texture control: blend until smooth, then stop before the body turns thin.
straws-stripes.serve: Serve hot in a clear 280–300 ml glass showing strawberry, chocolate and milk layers with strawberry cream on top.

i-put-a-spelt-on-you.description: Dark chocolate, spelt milk and a restrained spirulina note: grain-sweet, chocolate-led and green without tasting marine..

Ground dark chocolate for finish, 2 g

Spirulina as a slurry with cold spelt milk, then in — a restrained note.
Rest of the spelt milk. Heat to 60–70°C until glossy.
Serve before a skin forms. Chocolate leads; green is a hint.

what-s-up-brew.description: Cold brew coffee, dark chocolate ganache and ginger syrup shaken cold: coffee energy with cocoa body and ginger lift..

Dark ganache with ginger syrup, until smooth.
Filtered cold brew in. Shake until cold.
Fine-strain. Chocolate pearls. Serve cold.

Elderberry juice and cardamom. Rest of the yoghurt, until glossy.
Cocoa nibs. Serve cold.

berry-me-up.serve: Serve cold in a chilled 220–260 ml glass.

have-no-fear-beetroot-s-here.description: Warm beetroot juice, dark chocolate and whisky.

Dark chocolate with a splash of the juice, until glossy. Rest of the juice in.
Whisky in a warm glass.
Hot beetroot-chocolate over the whisky. Stir once.
Serve hot. Chocolate leads; beetroot is colour and depth.
have-no-fear-beetroot-s-here.serve: Serve hot in a warmed 220–240 ml glass or cup; mark clearly when whisky is added.

mango-django.description: Dark chocolate ganache and mango served cold in visible layers, with spice only when it supports the tropical chocolate finish..

Cardamom, chai spice or piri piri, 0.1–0.2 g

Dark ganache with a splash of mango, until smooth.
Rest of the mango. A hint of spice — lift, not heat.
Over a large ice ball. Serve cold. They may stir.

method: Chill the glass. Dairy stays cold.
Dark ganache in first.
Blueberries and flaxseed, blended into the texture.
Buttermilk gradually, until glossy.
Blueberries on top. Serve cold.

blueberry-thrills.serve: Serve in a chilled 260–280 ml glass, with a flaxseed rim when it is part of the service recipe.
